tom_dev: Hey CS/SRE  onboarding hit a weird combo: our Go serverless workers get valid tokens from our issuer but spawn from a small NAT pool so we see 401s interleaved with 429s. Pattern: cold-starts succeed, then some requests 401, other concurrent lambdas get immediate 429s. Anyone seen NAT/IP-based throttles + short-lived tokens before?
anya_cs: that sounds rough. Can you paste a micro-sequence of logs (sanitized) and say how many concurrent cold starts you see during deploy?
tom_dev: logs (sanitized):
```
[2026-03-20T10:01:01Z] GET /auth/token -> 200 {"tok":"ey..","exp":40}
[2026-03-20T10:01:02Z] POST /v1/chat -> 200
[2026-03-20T10:01:03Z] POST /v1/chat -> 401 {"err":"invalid_token"}
[2026-03-20T10:01:03Z] POST /v1/embeds -> 429 {"err":"rate_limit"} x 14
[2026-03-20T10:01:04Z] POST /v1/chat -> 429
```
tom_dev: we get ~120 concurrent cold starts hitting our egress NAT-sized pool of 10 IPs. Each lambda fetches its own token at init.
sam_sre: interesting surface: two orthogonal problems: 1) short token TTL + clock or timezone rounding can produce some 401s; 2) our rate limiter also has an IP-component to prevent abuse from a single egress IP. With many clients NATed behind few addresses you can hit per-IP burst thresholds and see 429s even if token-unique.
go-sdk: note from SDK folks: serverless patterns are special. Warmup often spawns many processes; per-instance token fetch + no connection reuse means many TLS handshakes and auth checks in a short window. For Go Lambdas we recommend centralizing token fetch in a lightweight initializer outside the hot path (one goroutine that caches token in /tmp or memory for other invocations to share) or use AWS provisioned concurrency to avoid cold starts. Example quick patch we recommend:```go
// pseudo
var cached = NewSingleflightCache()
func getToken() string { return cached.GetOrFetch(func(){ return fetchToken() }, 5*time.Second) }
```
anya_cs: short-term mitigations we can offer: 1) temporarily bump your tenant burst and per-ip allowances so warmup doesn't surface 429s; 2) try singleflight token cache and add tokenGraceMs (treat exp -= 5s); 3) add small randomized jitter (0-250ms) to cold-start init to avoid synchronized fanout. Want me to apply the temporary bump?
tom_dev: yes please  the staged rollout tomorrow will be less stressful if you bump. Also curious about server-side hints if IP-throttle triggered.
sam_sre: good ask  infra can add an extra response header when we decide to throttle due to egress-IP (e.g., `x-rate-reason: ip`), will open INFRA ticket. That helps customers identify NAT hotspots. In the meantime we can check logs for tenant+ip correlation.
quota-bot: @anya_cs increased tenant "copperfield" burst quota: +6 rps and raised temporary per-ip allowance for 48h (chg-id: N-66234).
tom_dev: applied singleflight cache + tokenGraceMs 5000 and added per-init jitter 0-200ms. After applying, 401s disappeared within a few minutes and 429s reduced to a handful of isolated retries. Thanks!
anya_cs: great  want me to capture this as an onboarding playbook note under "serverless cold-starts + NAT" (include: singleflight cache, tokenGraceMs, jitter, and request for temporary per-ip bump)? Also I'll flag renewals: "ramping, did temporary per-ip bump".
tom_dev: yes please capture that. We'll also evaluate provisioned concurrency and an egress-NAT expansion with our infra team.
go-sdk: follow-up: well add a SDK doc snippet recommending caching patterns and a short serverless cookbook. Also opening SDKGH-442 to show sample initializer code.
sam_sre: infra follow-up: will open INFRA-5582 to emit `x-rate-reason` for ip-based throttles and to surface tenant-ip aggregates to CS dashboards.
anya_cs: thanks team. Tom  ping us tomorrow during rollout and we can watch traces together.
tom_dev: will do  huge help, thanks all :raised_hands:
